title: A positive resolution of De Giorgi's conjecture in dimension eight
main_claim: Every entire solution u: R^8 -> (-1,1) of Δu = u^3 - u with ∂_8 u > 0 is a planar heteroclinic tanh((e·x - c)/√2). This is deduced (Jerison–Monneau/Savin-type blow-down, then a directed minimizing cone, then Wang's unit-density theorem) from Theorem 1.2: every bounded stable solution in R^7 is constant ±1 or planar, with no assumption on energy growth.

issues.description: The finite-density theorem for n=5,6,7 rests entirely on preliminary results quoted from Florit-Simon–Serra (arXiv v1): Thm 3.2, 3.4, Prop 3.6, 3.9–3.10, Def 3.7, Lemma 3.8, Sec 5 (sparse bad set), Thm 4.8, Lemmas 4.9–4.10. The paper says these are stated for n<=7. I could not check that claim from the sources here. If any of them is proved only for n=4, the reduction to an integer-density critical solution fails for n=5..7. This is a dependency risk, not a demonstrated gap.
issues.evidence: "These results explicitly assume n<=7, including Section 5 of that paper."

issues.description: The final step uses Wang 2017 Thm 11.1 (near-unit-density implies one-dimensional) as a black box, in every dimension and for the exact quartic normalization. I did not verify that it applies with the stated hypotheses (Modica bound plus density limit <= 1+δ_N). It is standard and probably correct.
issues.evidence: "The near-unit-density theorem of Wang [Theorem 11.1, p. 3036] says that, in every ambient dimension N, ..."

coverage:
I read all of 00-introduction, 00-classical, 02-monotone (Part I), 01-strategy, 01-diffuse and 02-finite-density in full. I read 06-radial in full apart from the proof details of the summable-errors lemma, which I skimmed. From 03-reach I read the penalty, the elementary chord bounds, the density window with delayed monotonicity, the start of isolation, the tangent phase ball, and Prop reach-calculus with its positive-foot transfer of multiplicity one. From 04-interface I read the exact exponential comparison (Steps 1–4 opening), clean log windows, and the sharp interaction constants (L12, L13). From 05-growth I read the M1 statement, the Simons/Kato step, the start of the gluing lemma, the reach multiplier, foot payments, the numerical reserve and the closure. Not read: the rest of the isolation parity projections, the 04-interface surface-stability lemmas (L1–L4, L11), most of the gluing proof, and the dimension-nine appendix.

Checked by computation (sympy/mpmath/numpy):
- q-stability identity Q(qη) = ∫q²|∇η|² − q³Dη²
- the extremal ODE solutions e^{±ay}(a ∓ tanh y)
- the conjugation of the D equation to ℒ0 = −Δ + 2 − G
- M(2) = 2 and M'(2) = 3/2; the derivative-to-mass ratio is at most 1/(2√2), with equality only at a = 2
- the identity H = ∂_νD/(2|p|²)
- the Hardy/Green coefficient contradiction √2 ≤ (3c*/4)(m−2), impossible for m ≤ 6
- the identity (−Δ+2)w = 3qw − q²D, and ∫e^{√2t}G² = 2σ, which gives the interaction constant 32
- tail coefficient 4 (q² ≤ 64e^{−√2ℓ}cosh²)
- the interpolant integral 32√2/tanh(3√2)
- C(G1) = 0.0832726 and the switching budget 0.08785 < 0.1
- the Laplacians of τ, h = ρ^{-2} and φ = ρ^{-4} on an m = 6 surface
- the λ/b' Hessian identity in R2
- all radial coefficient comparisons (3.474 > 3.44, 0.7095 < 0.72, 24 − 0.835·8·2.2 ≥ 5, 0.73·1.005/0.895 < 0.82)
- the curvature-charge total 0.714 < 0.73
- the error summations R3, R4, R5 (ε' ≈ 0.197)
- the multiplier numerics (A = 0.7675, limiting late coefficient 1/8, reserve ≥ 0.057I)
- that the curvature-induced defect mass gives exactly I/a² ≥ 1, so the claim I ≥ 0.999a² is sharp and consistent

As a consistency check, the finite-density inequality also fails at m = 7. That is fine: the barrier to n = 8 is the FSS reduction (Pacard–Wei examples), and the argument is lossy compared with the Gelfand threshold m ≥ 10.
